rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause requirement: local ordinance precedence and coverage
rules.requirement: The state just cause section does not apply to residential real property covered by a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or by a more protective local ordinance adopted or amended after September 1, 2019; in those cases the local ordinance applies, and no property is subject to both. Waivers of rights under the section are void.
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property, meaning any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including any dwelling or unit in a mobilehome park; not property covered by a qualifying local just cause ordinance, and not a homeowner of a mobilehome.
rules.exemptions: Property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019; property subject to a more protective local just cause ordinance adopted or amended after September 1, 2019; a homeowner of a mobilehome, as defined in Section 798.9.
rules.citation: Civil Code Section 1946.2 (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 203, Sec. 1 (AB 1529))
rules.penalty: The Attorney General, and the city attorney or county counsel where the unit is located, may seek injunctive relief based on violations of this section.
rules.quoted_span: (A) Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy adopted on or before September 1, 2019, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.
rules.interaction_text: (2) A residential real property shall not be subject to both a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy and this section.
